source_text: Quid tamen in hunc sensum afferamus attende. Etiamsi posses probare Adae peccatum filiis imputari, assentireris tamen aliorum parentum suboli eorum crimina non nocere.
pass_a_gloss: Attend nevertheless to what we bring into this sense. Even if you could prove that Adam's sin is imputed to sons, you would nevertheless assent that the crimes of other parents do not harm their offspring.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: Still, attend to what we bring against this view. Even if you could prove that Adam’s sin is charged to his children, you would nonetheless agree that other parents’ crimes do not harm their offspring (Deuteronomy 24:16).

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Continues the explicit argument from the law forbidding punishment of parents and children for one another’s sins.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
